tn_crack_of_doom_area.blurb: A cluster of 13 boulder problems within the Sternum section of Stone Fort, near Chattanooga. It is among the first groups of boulders you meet after leaving the front area and heading uphill along the trail that runs beside the golf course. The grades reach well past the beginner level: most problems fall between V3 and V7, with a couple of harder lines near V8 and one at V10, plus a few easier ones. The mix of crack climbing, rounded aretes and traverses suits climbers who already boulder at an intermediate or stronger level.

tn_ladies_delight.blurb: A wall on the Denny East side of Denny Cove, in the South Cumberland area near Jasper. It is the second wall you reach along the cliff line and carries 13 routes, 11 sport and 2 trad. The wall opens with short, technical arete moves, eases into slab, and finishes with a trad line in a cave. Most of the sport routes sit between 5.10 and 5.12, with a few easier trad and sport options on the lower end. It catches a lot of sun, though careful route choice can find reasonable shade.

tn_d_early_bird_wall.blurb: A sandstone wall in the Canyon at Pond Creek, in the Sequatchie Valley near Pikeville. It holds 13 routes, 10 sport and 3 trad, and is aimed at climbers comfortable from 5.10 into the 5.12 range, with one line above that. Expect roofs and sustained face climbing rather than easy warm-ups. The wall sits just below the stairs near the canyon's shop and stays in shade through the morning, until about noon, with some routes shaded later into the afternoon, which makes it a good early-day choice in warm weather.
